scope.note: Stablecoins left 153 user wallets that had granted infinite token approvals to the LI.FI aggregator contract (diamond); a facet added that morning forwarded caller-supplied call data without its whitelist check, so the contract spent standing approvals. No bridge escrow, liquidity pool or mint was involved. LI.FI names Ethereum and Arbitrum; DefiLlama's chain list (zkSync Era, Linea, Metis) does not match the on-chain record or LI.FI's report. Not a duplicate of DefiLlama's separate 2022-03-21 'LI.FI' record (an earlier approval outflow of about 0.6M).

Ethereum RPC (rpc.mevblocker.io): block 20318954, timestamp 2024-07-16T12:04:47Z, USDT Transfer of 5,383.52 to the recipient address (converted by me)

QuillAudits 9.7M (main recipient on Ethereum: 6,335,889 USDT, 3,191,914 USDC, 169,533 DAI) matches DefiLlama's 9.73M. Early estimates: 8M (Cyvers, PeckShield, Decurity), 8.7M held by the recipient (CertiK), 9M (The Block), 11M (CoinDesk update).

events.open_questions: (1) Whether the second address (1.80M USDC) and the two smaller users of the flaw are linked to the main recipient; LI.FI's 11.6M total appears to include the 1.80M. (2) Whether LI.FI posted on another channel before 13:41 UTC. (3) Whether affected users were reimbursed. (4) Basis of DefiLlama's chain list (zkSync Era, Linea, Metis): no transfers were checked on those chains; LI.FI's report names only Ethereum and Arbitrum. (5) Classification: O because the outflow was from approvals, not from bridge custody; DefiLlama labels it 'Token Approval Abuse'.

scope.note: A distinct event occurred: Poly Network's Neo N3 route (used by Flamingo Finance's f- and p-assets) was exploited on 11 Aug 2024 UTC (12 Aug in Asian time zones). The Neo N3 cross-chain manager contract (CCMC; Flamingo writes 'CMCC') executed each inbound message ten times and released Neo N3 assets from the bridge's pre-allocated supply; the initiating party bridged them back and drained the Ethereum-side lock proxy, with further requests to BSC and another Poly-connected chain. Not a duplicate of DefiLlama's 2023-07-02 'Poly Network' record (E21, also 5M; key-based forgery) or of the 2021-08-10 record (E05). Poly Network made no public statement; it had suspended new deployments in April 2024 and terminated all services on 30 Sep 2024.

release_side.share_note: Unbacked release on Neo N3 (pre-allocated f- and p-asset supply held by the bridge Proxy): 20 inbound messages from the party's own deposits (16 from Ethereum, 3 from BSC worth 221 BNB, 1 of 33,000 ONT from another Poly-connected chain) each paid out ten times. Redemption against escrow: Ethereum lock proxy 590 WETH, 1,168,460 USDT, 17.6 WBTC (its balances fell from 455.30 XWETH, 858,462.94 XUSDT and 13.37 XWBTC to 0.40, 0.94 and 0.07); requested but not read on chain: 526.9 fBNB to BSC and 363,000 pONT to the other chain. The rest of the f-assets was sold into Flamingo pools on Neo N3. Flamingo: the party took about 20-25% of all cross-chain asset funds, the amount held in the bridge's hot wallets; cross-chain f- and p-assets traded at about 75-80% of their underlying afterwards.

events.open_questions: (1) Why the CCMC executed each message ten times (replay check, re-entrancy through the recipient contract or another flaw); no technical post-mortem from Poly Network found. (2) BSC and third-chain releases (526.9 fBNB and 363,000 pONT requested) were not read on chain; Flamingo puts the BNB held at about 0.2M. (3) Why the 269.4 and 130 fWETH requests were never executed on Ethereum (no proof produced, relayer or Poly-chain control, or the party's choice). (4) Time of the Neo Council freeze and value frozen. (5) Whether any third party alerted before Flamingo; none found. (6) Value extracted from Flamingo pools by selling f-assets on Neo N3 is not separated in public figures.

scope.note: FEG (Feed Every Gorilla; DefiLlama lists it as 'Fegex') released FEG tokens from its own SmartBridge custody contract on Ethereum, Base and BSC after its relayer accepted cross-chain messages, carried over Wormhole, from an unauthorized source contract. The released FEG was sold into FEG/ETH and FEG/BNB pools (token price down about 99%). Wormhole's own contracts were not affected. DefiLlama's 1.07M matches the first public report (Docryt).
